source_meta.title: The AI revolution is coming – but what will it be like for you?
source_meta.author: The Guardian

passage_text: The rise of artificial intelligence is poised to reshape our world, but the specifics of this transformation remain a subject of intense debate. Some experts predict a future of unprecedented abundance and creativity, where AI handles mundane tasks, freeing humans to pursue higher-order goals. Others warn of mass unemployment and a new era of social inequality, as AI-powered automation displaces human workers across a wide range of industries.

questions.question_text: According to the passage, what is the primary point of contention regarding the rise of AI?
options: A) The speed of AI development.
B) The specific nature of the societal changes AI will bring.
C) The cost of implementing AI technology.
D) The ethical implications of AI.
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'the specifics of this transformation remain a subject of intense debate', indicating that the nature of the societal changes is the main point of contention.

supporting_offsets.snippet: the specifics of this transformation remain a subject of intense debate

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best synonym for 'ephemeral'?
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time, which is synonymous with fleeting.

passage_text: Déjà vu is a French term that literally means 'already seen.' It is a feeling of familiarity with a situation that is actually new. While the phenomenon is common, its underlying cause is not well understood. Some researchers believe it may be a memory anomaly, where a new experience is incorrectly stored in long-term memory, creating a false sense of familiarity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the memory anomaly theory of déjà vu?
options: A) People with memory disorders experience déjà vu more frequently.
B) Déjà vu is more common in younger people, whose memory systems are still developing.
C) A new brain imaging technique shows that the part of the brain responsible for familiarity is activated during déjà vu, while the part responsible for recollection is not.
D) The feeling of déjà vu can be induced by electrical stimulation of certain parts of the brain.
questions.explanation: The memory anomaly theory suggests that déjà vu is a memory error. If the part of the brain responsible for recollection is not activated, it would suggest that the feeling of familiarity is not due to a memory error, thus weakening the theory.

supporting_offsets.snippet: Some researchers believe it may be a memory anomaly, where a new experience is incorrectly stored in long-term memory, creating a false sense of familiarity.
